What Pima's NDT certificate tells Tucson job seekers about NAS 410 and SNT-TC-1A

Tucson is a rare US city where the local college states outright which aerospace standard its NDT classes serve. Pima Community College's Nondestructive Testing certificate, run from its Aviation Technology Center, says the classes meet only the academic requirements for NAS 410 Level II, and that students still need on-the-job training and their employer's tests to be fully certified. That one line describes the whole Tucson market: coursework builds evidence, and an employer's program issues the certification. Which program you end up in depends on whether you work on missile hardware, in an aircraft hangar or at a mine.

Missile hardware and the shops that feed it

RTX's Missiles & Defense business has its headquarters beside Tucson International Airport, and a supplier base around it machines, welds and tests precision parts. Defense aerospace orders commonly carry NAS 410 down from the prime, a pattern that dates from NAS 410 replacing MIL-STD-410, and suppliers usually see it named in their purchase-order quality clauses next to the method specifications. In that kind of shop a Responsible Level 3 approves the written practice, the course outlines and the examinations, and rules on what earlier training to credit. Penetrant, magnetic particle, ultrasonic and eddy current work on machined parts fills the day, and customer representatives may witness inspections or review the records behind them.

Hangars at Davis-Monthan, Marana and the airport

Aircraft maintenance divides three ways. Davis-Monthan Air Force Base and the 309th Aerospace Maintenance and Regeneration Group work under military technical orders and the service's own personnel rules. Civil maintenance, storage and reclamation shops, such as Ascent Aviation Services at Pinal Airpark in Marana and Bombardier's Tucson service center, follow the personnel standard written into their repair station manuals and customer contracts. FAA advisory circular AC 65-31B lists NAS 410, ATA Specification 105, SNT-TC-1A and EN 4179 among acceptable choices, so ask which one the manual names. Many local technicians enter as hangar assistants and are trained, logged and examined in-house, which makes a clean personal record even more important.

Copper mines and mills

ASARCO's Mission mine near Sahuarita and Freeport-McMoRan's Sierrita mine near Green Valley, with their mills, tanks and slurry lines, buy visual, magnetic particle and ultrasonic thickness work to structural, pressure-equipment and owner standards. Mine contractors and fabricators certify under written practices built on SNT-TC-1A. A technician can move from a mine contract to an aerospace shop, but the move means certification again under the new employer's program, usually after extra surface-method training. Utilities and power plants around Pima County sit on the same code-based side as the mines.

A file a Tucson RL3 can work with

  • Pima transcripts or other course records that show outlines and hours for each method.
  • An experience log signed by your supervisor, split by method and level.
  • Past general, specific and practical examination records, each marked with the standard it was taken under.
  • A current near-vision and color record.

An SNT-TC-1A certificate belongs in that file as evidence; on its own it never answers a NAS 410 requirement. NAS 410 also asks for more formal penetrant and magnetic particle training than SNT-TC-1A recommends, which is where most mine and plant technicians fall short. Quality managers at Tucson suppliers that also take mining or industrial orders should state the governing standard and revision on every certification and agree the move to NAS 410 Revision 6, released in December 2025, with their customers.

Atlantis and Southern Arizona

Atlantis courses follow ASNT SNT-TC-1A: theory self-paced online, Q&A with our ASNT NDT Level III (UT, RT, MT, PT, VT), practice in the Practical NDT hangar workplace and the hands-on practical at your employer's site. There is no Atlantis classroom in Tucson. Atlantis does not provide NAS 410 training, certification, examinations or a Responsible Level 3 in Southern Arizona. Whether any outside course counts toward a NAS 410 certification is your employer's RL3's decision, so ask before enrolling. Suppliers can use aerospace NDT consulting in Tucson for ASNT Level III support and written practices, and NAS 410 audit documentation prepared for the RL3 to approve. Compare the two schemes in NAS 410 vs SNT-TC-1A and read how NAS 410 certification works; for the surface methods, see magnetic particle testing training.
